newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Howard says Greenspan upbeat on U.S..
newsitem.headline: Australia's Howard says Greenspan upbeat on U.S..

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan told him in a recent meeting that the U.S. economy was stronger than he had ever seen and he saw no reason why the growth could not go on indefinitely.
"He said that the numbers in the American economy are stronger than he's ever seen and he sees no reason to believe that they won't go on indefinitely," Howard said in a radio interview on Monday.
"He's looking at an American economy which, in his own words, he can't understand all the reasons for its strength," Howard said.
Howard met Greenspan during an official visit to the United States almost two weeks ago.
He said the U.S. economic chief could not explain the strength of the U.S. economy, but had speculated it might be related to strong investment in technological change.
"... he said I think the full benefit of that technological change is now starting to feed through into a much better economy," Howard said.
The U.S. Federal Reserve last week opted to hold interest rates steady amid signs economic growth had slowed from a sizzling first quarter pace.
Second quarter economic growth in the United States cooled considerably from a strong first quarter, but most economists expect a resurgence.
